clue.text: Love tucking into awfully tall beer, ok?

indicators.note: tucking into says the love letter goes inside the scrambled beer letters
awfully says the words tall beer are badly jumbled into a new order

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a tall glass of beer is acceptable, with a lover nestled into it somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges TALL BEER, and 'tucking into' puts O inside those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tolerable is passable or just about acceptable, which is what 'ok' conveys.

clue.text: He lost cat to tumble dryers

indicators.note: to tumble says the letters of he lost cat fall into a new arrangement, as clothes do in a tumble dryer

explanation.surface: A man has lost his cat, which has gone into the tumble dryer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumble dryers' reads as one appliance, but 'to tumble' is the anagram signal and 'dryers' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea cloths are used in the kitchen for drying washed dishes, so they are dryers.

clue.text: Maiden cut into pork pies and fruit

indicators.note: cut into says the maiden letter is set inside the slang word

parts.note: pork pies is Cockney rhyming slang for lies
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman slices into pork pies and some fruit for a picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, 'pork pies' means lies; a pork pie is a British cold meat pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Limes are small green citrus fruits.

clue.text: Soviet film about Scottish island swimmer

indicators.note: about says the Soviet-plus-film letters go round the island

parts.note: Soviets were called Reds
E.T. is Spielberg's famous film
Mull is an island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A Soviet movie set on a Hebridean island features someone swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' is crossword shorthand for a fish; Mull is a Scottish island off the west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The red mullet is a fish, and a fish is a crossword's classic swimmer.

clue.text: Dance and drink? That could be a mistake!

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Going to a dance and drinking might well lead to an embarrassing error.
explanation.definitionFit: A balls-up is British slang for a bungled job or blunder.

clue.text: I raced about with half-cut cads to see stimulating art

indicators.note: about says I and the word for raced are turned back to front

parts.note: tore means raced, as in tore down the road

indicators.note: half-cut says only the first half of the word cads is kept

explanation.surface: Someone races around with drunken cads to visit a racy art show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses I TORE to make EROTI; 'half-cut' (also slang for tipsy) keeps CA of CADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is art or literature intended to arouse sexual desire.

clue.text: Wee guy's indignant reply to charge of greed in hearing?

indicators.note: in hearing says the outraged retort is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.words: indignant reply to charge of greed
parts.note: accused of being greedy, one might protest 'Pig? My!'

explanation.surface: A small man responds angrily when accused of greed at a tribunal hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' poses as a legal hearing but signals a sound-alike: 'Pig? My!' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pygmy is a very small person, and 'wee' is Scottish for small.

clue.text: Hoskins must be hugged by model? Cool!

indicators.note: must be hugged by says the setter's letter sits inside the model word

parts.note: to model is to pose
Hoskins is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The setter hopes a model will embrace him, which would be cool.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for I, the setter speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise is calm composure, the quality of keeping cool under pressure.

clue.text: New model glad to get top award

indicators.note: new says the letters of model glad are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A newcomer to modelling is pleased to win a top prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold medal is awarded for first place, the highest prize in a competition.

clue.text: Desire to grab yours truly in a really hot place

indicators.note: to grab says the desire word holds the me letters inside it

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: Someone longs to seize the speaker while somewhere sweltering.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen, on the Arabian Peninsula, is a country with an extremely hot climate.

clue.text: Member a Green brought into party is a beast

parts.note: an arm is a member, or limb, of the body

indicators.note: brought into says the sick word goes inside the party word

parts.note: a do is a party
green can mean sickly or ill

explanation.surface: A Green Party member is introduced into a political party, described as a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks political but means looking ill.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured mammal of the Americas, so it is a beast.

clue.text: I harshly criticise one of the big religions

parts.note: to slam is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: The speaker condemns one of the world's major faiths.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is among the world's largest faiths, alongside Christianity and Hinduism.

clue.text: You must follow Scottish girl in slow part of dance

indicators.note: must follow says the you letter comes after the girl word

parts.note: lass is a Scottish word for a girl
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A partner must follow a Scottish girl's lead during the slow section of a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The lassu is the slow opening section of the Hungarian csárdás.

clue.text: Superhero spotted a dude in need of picking up

indicators.note: in need of picking up says the phrase is caught by the ear, picking up being hearing

parts.note: spotted a dude means spied a man

explanation.surface: A superhero sees a guy who needs rescuing or lifting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking up' suggests a pick-up line or rescue, but means hearing: 'spied a man' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spider-Man is the Marvel Comics superhero Peter Parker.

clue.text: Tart will have sex covered in cream

indicators.note: covered in says the sex word is wrapped by the cream word

parts.note: the cream is the top, the best part
a roll in the hay is sex, so roll can stand for it

explanation.surface: A cream tart is offered, with a racy hint about sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' reads as a pastry beside 'cream' but is the slang for a promiscuous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollop and tart are both dated, derogatory words for a promiscuous woman.

clue.text: Work with Eurocentric leader helping campaign

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: leader says only the first letter of Eurocentric is used

parts.note: a ration is a helping or allowance

explanation.surface: Someone works with a Europe-focused leader to help a political campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A military campaign is an operation, an organised action.

clue.text: Give up a prohibition mafia boss

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
a don is a Mafia boss

explanation.surface: A mafia boss is told to give up because of Prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon something is to give it up entirely.

clue.text: Any bedpan having been upset is an objectionable thing

indicators.note: having been upset says the letters of any bedpan are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A spilled bedpan is something no one wants to deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad penny is an idiom for an unwelcome person or thing that keeps turning up.

clue.text: Junkie knight painter possibly keeps company

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: keeps says the artist word holds the company letters within it

parts.note: a painter is one example of an artist

explanation.surface: A drug-addicted knight who perhaps paints keeps people company.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotist is an addict of narcotic drugs, a junkie.

clue.text: Promise to keep a hold of extremely tense jumper

indicators.note: to keep a hold of says the promise word grips the next letters inside it

parts.note: to swear is to promise

indicators.note: extremely says only the outer letters of tense are used

explanation.surface: Someone vows to cling tightly to a very tight-fitting jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is British for a knitted pullover, not someone who jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a jumper is a sweater, a knitted top pulled over the head.

clue.text: Old US singer wearing graduation clothes?

parts.note: graduates wear robes at the ceremony
if you have something on, you are wearing it

explanation.surface: An old American singer is pictured in academic gowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Robeson was an American bass-baritone singer, famous for Ol' Man River.

clue.text: Bootlicker? Bend over with hands around heel of shoe!

indicators.note: over says the bend word is flipped back to front

parts.note: an arc is a bend or curve

indicators.note: around says the two hand letters enclose what follows

parts.note: L and R are the left and right hands

indicators.note: heel of says the last letter of shoe is taken

explanation.surface: A grovelling instruction: bend down and clutch the heel of someone's shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses ARC; 'around' puts L and R around E.
explanation.definitionFit: A crawler is a toady who fawns on superiors, the same as a bootlicker.

clue.text: Revolutionary against Republican performing V-sign?

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
V is short for versus, against
a performer on stage is on

explanation.surface: A revolutionary opposing a Republican makes a rude two-fingered gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is a V-shaped stripe or symbol, so it is a sign shaped like a V.

clue.text: Flexible secretary lawyer's taken over desk

indicators.note: taken over says the secretary and lawyer letters are turned around

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
DA is a district attorney, a lawyer; the 's is lawyer is
a desk is a kind of table

explanation.surface: An adaptable secretary finds the lawyer has commandeered her desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken over' reverses PA DA to give ADAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adaptable means being able to adjust to new conditions, as a flexible person does.

clue.text: Some grandpas cottaging in a racy English town?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Elderly men engage in illicit encounters in a racy English town.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition included 'in', which is a link word, so the definition starts at 'a'. 'racy' means home to horse racing: Ascot is a Berkshire town famous for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a Berkshire town known for its racecourse, so it is 'racy' as in having races.

clue.text: Lacerations and things they can create?

definitions.meaning: ..., rhyming with bears, are rips or cuts
..., rhyming with fears, are the crying that painful wounds can bring on

explanation.surface: Cuts and the crying they might cause.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling gives rips in flesh and the drops of weeping that injury provokes.

clue.text: I love to chase old man close to nudist courtyard

indicators.note: to chase says the I and love letters follow behind the others

parts.note: pa is father, the old man

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of nudist

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: The speaker chases an elderly man near a nudist in a courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor area or inner courtyard of a house.

clue.text: Those heading to army encampment: brigade on exercise?

indicators.note: those heading means the leading letters of the words that follow are taken

explanation.surface: Soldiers heading to an army camp find the brigade doing exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Tae Bo is a fitness workout combining aerobics with kickboxing moves.

clue.text: Popular to tuck into tea here?

indicators.note: to tuck into says the popular word is put inside the tea word

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Is this the popular place to eat a tea?
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' suggests eating, but is the insertion signal; 'here?' points to where tea comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: China is the homeland of tea drinking, so it is a place where tea is drunk.

clue.text: Plain green ties needing to be done up

indicators.note: needing to be done up says the letters of green ties must be rearranged and fixed

explanation.surface: Plain green ties need knotting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective for the ties but is the definition, a flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast grassland plain in Tanzania and Kenya.

clue.text: I butt flipping soprano to get foreign capital

indicators.note: flipping says I and the butt word are turned around

parts.note: to nut someone is slang for head-butting them

explanation.surface: Someone head-butts an annoying soprano to win foreign money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British oath but reverses I NUT to TUNI. 'capital' seems to be money but is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia.

clue.text: One nursing tot got a drunk to be an animal

parts.note: a nanny looks after a small child

indicators.note: drunk says the letters of got a stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A nanny got a drunk to behave like a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny goat is a female goat, which is an animal.
